hints: Focus on Le Chatelier's principle here. To get more solid, you need to push this dissolving equilibrium back to the left.
Notice the ions on the right are $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ and $\text{OH}^-$. Increasing any one of these by common ion effect will shift the equilibrium left.
Consider which added compound will make more $\text{OH}^-$ in water, and which ones will make $\text{H}^+$ that removes $\text{OH}^-$ and $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$.
walkthrough:
**Understand what more solid means**

Think of this as a dissolving tug of war. More solid means the equilibrium has shifted to the left, back towards reactants.

$$\text{Ca}_5(\text{PO}_4)_3\text{OH(s)} \rightleftharpoons 5\text{Ca}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 3\text{PO}_4^{3-}\text{(aq)} + \text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}$$

**Apply Le Chatelier with common ions**

Adding a product ion will push the position left. So adding $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ or $\text{OH}^-$ will give more solid.

Removing a product ion, for example by reacting it away, will pull the position right and dissolve more solid.

**Check acid-base behaviour of each additive**

Ammonia is a base in water and makes extra hydroxide:
$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$$
That extra $\text{OH}^-$ is a common ion, so the equilibrium shifts left and more $\text{Ca}_5(\text{PO}_4)_3\text{OH(s)}$ precipitates. Acids do the opposite, they provide $\text{H}^+$ which removes $\text{OH}^-$ to make water and protonates $\text{PO}_4^{3-}$ to $\text{HPO}_4^{2-}$, so they dissolve the solid.

options.A: NH3 acts as a base to increase [OH-]. This common ion pushes the solubility equilibrium to the left by Le Chatelier's principle, so more solid Ca5(PO4)3OH forms.
options.B: NH4Cl provides NH4+, which is acidic. It donates H+ to remove OH- and to protonate PO4(3-), pulling the equilibrium to the right and dissolving more solid, not precipitating it.
options.C: CH3CO2H is an acid that releases H+. The H+ neutralises OH- to water and converts PO4(3-) to HPO4(2-) or H2PO4-, so product ions are removed and the equilibrium shifts right to dissolve the solid.
options.D: NaCl gives Na+ and Cl-, which are spectator ions here. They do not react with Ca2+, PO4(3-) or OH-, so they have no effect on the equilibrium position.
